claim: The pipeline converts policy sections into separate questions and reports whether each was followed.
The demo uses the public Enron email corpus as repeatable input data.
Each policy result can include a description or evidence rather than only a binary label.
The speakers compare one broad reusable check with more specialized policy checks.
A proposed dashboard lets humans review flagged emails and decide whether each flag is correct.
Repeated human judgments can become a better evaluation set for future prompt changes.
The final discussion says an unlabeled flagged email would have been useless for evaluating the system.
note: Caption wording is imperfect, but the review context supports this reading.
